slot_note: ETL lane, architecture 3: a re-root at stage 1 of architecture 2 (a labour force survey's unemployment rate restated across a questionnaire redesign phased in through rotation groups), whose main call held but whose ask layer could not be repaired inside that world's records; new world (crematoria mercury from dental amalgam), new dataset, new generator and new shell, chosen so the ask layer rides crematoria operations records the call never reads
niche: a provincial crematoria mercury fund certifying whether its 2026 scheme year met the regulation's 55 per cent abatement share and designating which unabated crematoria must fit abatement by 2028, each cremation's mercury read from the decedent's dental amalgam by birth cohort across the national adult oral health survey's 1996, 2006 and 2016 waves
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the province's cremation permits, every crematorium's abatement commissioning dates and the oral health survey's three waves correctly, and reads the regulation, estimates each 2026 cremation's mercury from the 2016 survey's amalgam teeth at the decedent's age at death (the inventory's age-based method), or carries each cohort from 2016 along that same age profile, which returns identical figures, and so files the abated share and the designations that the age profile gives, not those each decedent's cohort carried along its own change between the 2006 and 2016 waves gives.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the mercury in the dental amalgam of each person cremated, estimated the way an emissions inventory builds a cremation source from a national oral health survey: each decedent's amalgam read from their birth cohort and carried along that cohort's own change between the survey's waves to the year of death; with hospital-waste or landfill nouns there is no amalgam carried by a birth cohort, no survey wave and no ageing within a cohort, and the share and the designations stop parsing.
layer1: the survey's three waves published as PDF tables whose layouts change by wave (age bands, sex splits and the top band differ)
the province's cremation permits keyed by permit number with age at death in completed years and a crematorium code that changed when two operators merged
each crematorium's abatement plant commissioned on its own date, some during the scheme year, so a crematorium is abated for only part of 2026
operators' own registers, cremator controller logs and abatement plant logs in their own layouts and clocks (for the asks)
distractors: post-abatement stack test reports and the province's deaths by place of occurrence
stakeholder_role: the Fund's technical secretary, who compiles the annual mercury return and the designation proposal for the trustees

spine.entity: one cremation permit issued and used in 2026

world.geography: Canada (an unnamed province; the Fund, its regulation, the crematoria and the survey are fictional; personas on the en_CA index)
world.org_type: a statutory not-for-profit crematoria mercury fund and its member crematoria, municipal and private

driver: The decisive quantity is a per-member property carried by each member's birth cohort and measured only in repeated cross-sections of the living population taken years before the period the decision reads; one cross-section's age profile runs across cohorts, so applying it at each member's age in that period, or carrying each cohort forward along that same profile, returns earlier cohorts' values, and only each cohort's own change between the cross-sections carries it to the period, which reorders the units whose members differ in age.
driver_concrete: Each 2026 cremation releases the mercury in the dental amalgam of the person cremated, which follows the person's birth cohort (those born from the mid-1940s to the late 1950s carry the most amalgam, earlier cohorts lost their teeth, later ones grew up with fluoride), and the national adult oral health survey measured cohorts only in 1996, 2006 and 2016; applying the 2016 survey's age profile at each decedent's age at death, or ageing each cohort along that profile, gives the 2016 values of older cohorts and overweights crematoria whose decedents died in their sixties, so the abated share and the designation order are read from each decedent's cohort carried from 2016 along its own change since 2006.
stump: A competent analyst applies the 2016 survey's amalgam at each decedent's age at death (or ages each cohort along that profile, which returns the same figures) and files the abated share and the designations that profile gives; counting cremations files another; only each decedent's cohort carried from 2016 along its own change since 2006 gives the golden share and designations.

differentiation.task480: task480 reads each vehicle's current-year mileage from one lifetime cumulative total, whose average over a vehicle's life overstates a yearly increment that falls with age; task453 has no per-unit record at all: a property each person carries from their birth cohort is measured only in survey cross-sections years earlier, and the cross-section's age profile runs across cohorts, so it is re-keyed to each decedent's cohort and aged along that cohort's own change between waves
differentiation.task453: v2 restated a survey's published rate across a questionnaire redesign read within month in sample; v1 removed a dated placement step before seasonal factors; v3 has no change in measurement, no phase-in and no seasonal adjustment: an emissions inventory reads each cremation's mercury from a cohort-carried property measured in earlier survey waves

lineage.fate: shipped 2026-10-14 (judge DETERMINISTIC, APPROVE; delivered, pending review) and reshipped 2026-11-01 under the leak gate; its main call held at the judge (Gate H decisive step analytical), but its ask layer measured spent on 2026-11-01 (the honest careful-solver cracker keeps 10 of 10: a dwelling is the sample reference plus its entry month) and could not be repaired inside the world's records (2026-11-02: the re-site and the full household-roster replacement both measured spent, since every survey mechanic the records turn on is filed for the call and the unfiled ones are identities a member-repeat check recovers); re-rooted 2026-11-02 to a new world, dataset, generator and shell.
lineage.driver: The size of a change in how a rotating panel is measured has to be read from the months in which only the units newest to the panel received the new measurement, while every unit's answers drift with how many times it has been asked, so the two arms' difference carries that drift; and the change acts differently on a unit's first answer than on its later ones, so the change in the published figure, which averages every occasion equally, is the mean of the per-occasion effects, each read against the same occasion before the change, which neither the arms' difference nor one effect with the occasion held fixed returns.
lineage.driver_concrete: The redesigned questionnaire went only to dwellings entering the sample from July 2025, so in each phase-in month (July to November 2025) its arm is dwellings on their first interviews and the previous arm dwellings on their last, and first interviews always read high (rotation-group bias); its dependent interviewing works only from a dwelling's second interview, so the change in the published rate, which averages the six rotation groups, is the mean of the six month-in-sample effects, each read against the same month in sample before July 2025.
lineage.shell: whether / Put ... in / determination PDF and a restated-series CSV

lineage.fate: shipped 2026-10-13 (judge pass 1 DETERMINISTIC, APPROVE) and re-rooted 2026-10-14 at the author's request for a stronger stump: the decisive step (the January 2026 placement step removed as a level shift before the seasonal factors) is a dated step an event study finds, and the hardening that would have hidden it (the canneries' 2021 to 2023 reclassification) was judged NOT_DETERMINISTIC, SEND_BACK, as a fork between direct and indirect adjustment, and reverted.
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity compares two periods that both lie after a documented change in where the source places what it counts, so the change looks irrelevant, but the seasonal pattern used to adjust them is estimated from a history spanning it, and an adjustment that does not first remove the change as a level shift lets it leak into the seasonal factors and moves the latest period most where the change was largest, in either direction.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each region's first-quarter 2027 seasonally adjusted payroll jobs are set against its 2026 average, both on the workplace placement the revenue agency's statistics have used since January 2026, when jobs that had sat at employers' account addresses (head offices in Wickmoor and Saltmere) moved to their mines, mills, plants, hospitals and stores; a default seasonal adjustment estimates the seasonal pattern across that step, pulling the quarter down in the regions that gained (Kestrow North, Varrenby Shore) and up in the Capital, while official practice removes the step as a level shift in the regARIMA pre-adjustment (or restates the earlier history) before the seasonal filters run.

notes: Re-rooted 2026-11-02 (architecture 3). The ETL move is re-keying a survey's age-by-wave tables onto the decedents' birth cohorts and ageing them along each cohort's own trajectory; reading the tables correctly is not sufficient because the easy re-key (age at death, or ageing along one wave's profile) is algebraically the same cross-section. The decision reads a closed year (2026) because the regulation tests each scheme year after it closes; the designation it triggers is forward (abatement by 2028). Guard at the draw: WARN overuse.domain (physical-environmental-sciences in 5 of the last 12; emissions-inventory is the only task type that serves ETL for a cremation source) and WARN shell.repeat read off architecture 2's prompt.txt still on disk (the architecture 3 prompt redraws the shell). Pattern none with G6 decisive: the cohorts shifted under the survey's age profile.
